issue.title: [BUG] Native grep reports success and "0 matches" when stat/readdir/readFile fail

steps: Create a file named readable.txt containing the single line `needle`.
Use the grep tool to search for 'needle' in the path does-not-exist.
expected: Searching a path that does not exist returns a file-not-found error (or at least says the path was not searched) instead of a normal empty result.
defect: The grep tool returns the normal successful summary `0 matches across 0 files`, indistinguishable from a real search with no hits.

fault location.explanation: Resolves the search target with filesystem.stat(searchPath) inside a try block whose failure is not reported; PR #24053 (commit d7f0579) reports a missing/unreadable target instead.

`catch { filePaths = []; }` turns any stat failure (e.g. ENOENT for does-not-exist) into an empty file list, so the tool prints `0 matches across 0 files` with success; PR #24053 surfaces the error (and counts skipped paths) instead.

Directory walk swallows readdir failures (`catch { return []; }`), and the readFile batch at lines 372-377 likewise returns undefined for unreadable files, so partial searches look complete; PR #24053 records these as skipped/unreadable in the summary (or throws in strict mode).

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/24053 (commit d7f0579a0445469430b9eadbf9c28ed3fa009839). In the tested source, grepTool.execute in packages/core/src/workspace/tools/grep.ts wraps target resolution in try { const stat = await filesystem.stat(searchPath); ... } catch { filePaths = []; }, so a path that does not exist (or cannot be stat'ed) silently becomes an empty file list; the directory walk swallows readdir errors with `catch { return []; }`, file reads swallow readFile errors and are skipped, and loadGitignore swallows any error. None of these reach the outer error handler, so the tool returns the ordinary `0 matches across 0 files` summary and ends its span as successful, leading the agent to conclude the content does not exist. The fix replaces grepTool with createGrepTool({ strict }), distinguishes ENOENT/ENOTDIR from other errors, reports missing targets and skipped unreadable directories/files in the summary (or throws when strict), and narrows loadGitignore's catch to a missing file. The fix is first released in mastracode@0.41.0 / @mastra/core@1.68.0, which is exactly the pinned revision, so the case is tested at mastracode@0.40.0 (the last release before the fix), which still has the swallowing catches.
